sam_r: Quick sync: onboarding Horizon-14B int6. Ran targeted safety needles + medical QA. Noting anomalous spike in soft-refusal on medQA. Dropping results and next steps here.

sam_r: `run_eval --model horizon-14b-int6 --suite medqa-v2 --seed 7 --save s3://redwood-evals/hz14b-int6-medqa-seed7.json`

eval-bot: eval complete | medqa_refusal=0.11 (fp16 baseline 0.03) | jb_pass=0.095 (fp16 0.07) | avg_tox=0.003 | artifact: s3://redwood-evals/hz14b-int6-medqa-seed7.json :information_source:

maya_p: 0.11 refusal is high. First checklist: tokenization parity, decoding config, qconfig. Any compile warnings?

jin: Token ids identical to fp16 run. Found that int6 defaulted to lowlat decoding (top_k=6). fp16 used top_k=40. Also qconfig used per_tensor, clamp=0.025.

nisha: Per-tensor quant can smear channel-level distributions. Try per-channel + relaxed clamp. Also re-run with decoding parity first.

sam_r: Re-ran with top_k=40 only: `run_eval --model horizon-14b-int6 --decoding "top_k=40,temp=0.8" --suite medqa-v2`

eval-bot: re-run done | medqa_refusal=0.037 | jb_pass=0.081 | avg_tox=0.0032 | notes: decoding parity sharply reduced refusals; remaining jb delta small. artifact: s3://redwood-evals/hz14b-int6-topk40.json

maya_p: That suggests decoding was the larger effect. Still want to try per-channel qconfig sweep [clamp=0.02,0.05]. Jin, can you run clamp=0.05 per_channel and dump logits diff for needles 42/57?

jin: On it. Also noticed a minor KV-cache padding alignment warning in the compile log for the default build; filing a follow-up with eng-runtime incase it affects edge cases.

nisha: Plan: AB test matrix on staging routes: fp16 vs int6(decoding parity) vs int6(per_channel+clamp0.05). Sample 500 inferences each, human-review 200 failure cases. Set alert: jb_pass > 0.10 or refusal > 0.06 -> page.

sam_r: I'll create RW ticket RW-3719 with artifacts and schedule the canary tomorrow 09:00 PT. Thanks all.
